# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service

|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.

may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt
    |  |--os_detection_scan.txt

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Attempt operating system detection.

are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |

| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

    |--README.md

    |  |--basic_scan.txt

- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt
    |  |--os_detection_scan.txt
    |  |--test_service_scan.txt
    |  |__nmap_scan_results.txt

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.

### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished

as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

    |  |--basic_scan.txt

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service

|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with

- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt
    |  |--os_detection_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
    |  |--service_version_scan.txt

# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished

as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.

  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service

| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1

only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished

|---|---|---|---|

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Basic Network Scanning with Nmap

## Internship Task 1 - Cybersecurity

##1. Overview

This project demonstrates basic network scanning using Nmap
on Kali Linux. It documents open ports, service identification,
operating system detection, and basic security analysis in an authorized
local test environment.

##2. Objectives

- Perform a basic Nmap scan.
- Identify services and versions with service detection
- Attempt operating system detection.
- Document open ports and assess potential security risks.
- Capture screenshots and save scan output for evidence.

##3. Tools and Environment

- Kali Linux
- Nmap 7.99
- Python 3 HTTP server for a controlled test
- Kali Linux Terminal

##4. Installation

Nmap is included in the Kali Linux environment used for this project.

To check the installed version:

        nmap --version

On Kali Linux, if Nmap is missing and package repositories
are configured, install it using:

        sudo apt update
        sudo apt install map

For Windows, use the official Nmap download page:
https://nmap.org/download.html

##5. Commands Used

## Basic Scan

   nmap 127.0.0.1

Scans Nmap's default set of TCP ports on the local machine.


### Service and version detection

     nmap -sV 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify services and their versions on detected open ports


### Operating System detection

     sudo nmap -O 127.0.0.1

Attempts to identify the target operating system using 
network responses. Results may be inconclusive when scanning localhost.

### Controlled HTTP service test

Start a local test server in a terminal:


  python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1


In another terminal, scan the test port:

  nmap -sV -p 8000 127.0.0.1

The server is bound to the loopback interface and is intended
only for local testing. Stop it with Ctrl+C when finished


##6. Findings

### Initial localhost scan

The basic scan reported all 1,000 default-scanned TCP ports
as closed. No open ports were identified in that scan.

OS detection was inconclusive because multiple OS fingerprints matched the response.


### Controlled Test Service


| Port | State | Service | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8000/tcp | Open | HTTP | SimpleHTTPServer 0.6 (Python 3.13.12) |

This result came from the deliberately started local python
HTTP server, not from a pre-existing exposed service.

##7. Security Analysis

The Python HTTP server is useful for development and testing,
but it is not intended to be a hardened production server.
Depending on its configuration and working directory, files 
may be accessible to clients that can reach it.

Recommended precautions:

- Bind test services to 127.0.0.1 when only local access is needed
- Do not serve directories containing confidential files.
- Stop temporary services after testing.
- Expose services to a network only when necessary and with 
  suitable access controls.

## 8. Project Structure


    nmap-internship/
    |--README.md
    |--reports/
    |  |--basic_scan.txt
